name: Card in, card out: a ticketless transient stay, paid at the exit
description: Lakeside Garage runs ticketless credit-card-in/card-out on lane 1. A driver taps a card at entry; the lane holds $50.00. At the exit it captures the real fee, after a mis-keyed amount is refused. A cleanup script cannot void a captured payment, and a partial refund for a validation that was missed needs a supervisor. One PaymentRecord carries the whole story (Part 13 §13.1, §13.1a).

steps.name: Lane 1, 10:10: a card instead of a ticket
steps.narration: Card-in/card-out is the most common ticketless transient flow: the card is the ticket. At entry the lane authorizes a hold; at exit it captures what the stay actually cost. APX models both as one PaymentRecord with a capture status (Part 13).

steps.name: Entry: the lane holds $50.00
steps.narration: The lane controller records the authorization with captureLater: true. The record is approved but only authorized: no money has been collected yet. The Idempotency-Key is built from the lane, the time and the card, so a retry cannot place a second hold.

steps.name: The supervisor's list of open holds
steps.narration: At any time the night supervisor can list holds that have not been captured. This is how a garage finds cars that are still inside on a card.

steps.name: An older console sees nothing collected
steps.narration: A console written before capture status existed looks the ticket up and finds no payment. That is the rule, not an accident: a hold is invisible unless the query asks for captureStatus=authorized, so an older client cannot count it as revenue (§13.1a).

steps.name: 16:15: exit, and a mis-keyed fee
steps.narration: Six hours later the car reaches the exit. The fee is mis-keyed as $125.00, more than the hold. The server refuses the capture with 422 and says why, rather than taking an amount the driver never authorized.

steps.name: The real fee is captured: $12.50
steps.narration: The corrected capture takes $12.50 and releases the rest of the hold. The same record is now captured, with the collected amount and time.

steps.name: A cleanup script tries to void it
steps.narration: A nightly script that voids stale holds picks this one up by mistake. A captured payment cannot be voided; it can only be refunded. The 409 payment-state-illegal problem says so, and the money stays where it is.

steps.name: Now the console sees the payment
steps.narration: The plain ticket lookup that saw nothing at noon now finds the captured $12.50.

steps.name: The driver calls: a validation was missed
steps.narration: The driver had a $4.00 restaurant validation the lane never applied. The agent tries to refund it. At this garage refunds need a supervisor, and a request with no approval evidence is refused with 403 approval-required (§13.1a).

body.reason: restaurant validation not applied at the exit lane

steps.name: With the supervisor's approval, refunded
steps.narration: The agent gets the shift supervisor's approval and sends it with the refund. The record keeps the original $12.50 and adds refundedAmount $4.00, so the books show both the charge and the correction. It stays approved; it would become reversed only if the whole amount were refunded (§13.1a).

body.reason: restaurant validation not applied at the exit lane

approval.note: validation receipt photographed by the driver

steps.name: What subscribers were told
steps.narration: Two events, not three. apx.accounts.payment.recorded.v1 is never published for a hold: it goes out first at capture, then again when the refund changed refundedAmount, each time with the full current record (§13.1a, §13.4). The accounting system never sees the $50.00 that was only held.
